entities.title: Nothing checks that the client's rules agree with the server's
entities.summary: The client judges games with rules.gd and the server with chess.js (shared/rules.ts); the two are tested separately and never against each other.
entities.compromise: The Godot client has its own GDScript rules instead of the server's; rules.gd says it is "the same rules", and only each side's own tests back that.
entities.cost: Where they differ (insufficient material, SAN, or a draw rule), the client shows a result, a move or a hint the server disagrees with: an online move it lets the player make is refused, or a game against the computer it ends is refused by POST games/computer as not over.
acceptanceCriteria: A check plays the same move lists through rules.gd and shared/rules.ts and compares legal moves, SAN and results, or the client uses the server's judgement.

origin.description: The class comment: the server judges with chess.js; this is the same rules for the board.
